description: Recomputes a PIN-RECORD flow (precommit -> conformance-run -> optional repair-run) from raw inputs: git-authorship disjointness (C2, a checkable floor -- proves disjoint repository attribution, not full person/control/toolchain independence), precommit_hash as sha256(JCS(the whole predicate-precommit.v0 record)) (C3, closes the delimiter-free-concatenation collision surface -- naive sha256(hash_a + hash_b + hash_c) is ambiguous at variable-length boundaries), set-valued attribution canonicalization (dedupe + sort-by-JCS-byte-order before hashing, since plain JCS key-sorts objects but leaves array order semantic), and a verdict enum {PASS, CONFORMANCE_FAILED, UNRESOLVED} where disagreement and inability-to-determine are distinct terminal states, reason required iff UNRESOLVED (C4). Repair is a bound recomputing run (C5), never a stored boolean. Deliberately out of scope: C1 (git ancestry of precommit-introducing-commit before run_identity) -- a fact about repository history a vectors-based gate cannot check, belongs in a real CI step against a real repo.
recompute: disjointness_holds = mutant.author_identity != predicate.oracle_author_identity ; precommit_hash = sha256(JCS(predicate-precommit.v0 record)) ; verdict = PASS if canonical(A_i)==canonical(observed), CONFORMANCE_FAILED if both present and differ, UNRESOLVED (with reason) if either missing

vectors.name: clean-disjoint-pass
vectors.note: mutant and predicate authored by different, disjoint parties; the gate's observed attribution matches A_i exactly -- PASS, and independence holds at its real (checkable-floor) strength.

vectors.name: same-author-disjointness-violation
vectors.note: mutant and predicate authored by the SAME identity -- disjointness_holds is false (a real, mechanically-caught independence-floor violation), reported as its own fact, separate from the conformance verdict (which still computes normally on its own inputs).

vectors.name: set-valued-attribution-order-independence
vectors.note: A_i is a set (member order not semantic). The gate's observed set is the SAME members in a DIFFERENT order -- canonical(A_i) must still match, so this is PASS, proving the dedupe+sort-then-JCS fix actually normalizes order (a naive per-array JCS would wrongly report CONFORMANCE_FAILED here).

vectors.name: unresolved-no-observation
vectors.note: The gate under test never produced an observation (crashed, timed out, or genuinely could not run) -- UNRESOLVED/no_observation, NOT silently treated as a pass, NOT collapsed into CONFORMANCE_FAILED (which would falsely claim a determinate disagreement that never happened).

vectors.name: conformance-failed-real-disagreement
vectors.note: The gate under test genuinely disagrees with A_i (both exist, both determinate, both differ) -- CONFORMANCE_FAILED, the honest determinate-disagreement state, distinct from UNRESOLVED.

vectors.name: repair-run-restores-pass
vectors.note: The original run mismatched (CONFORMANCE_FAILED); a repair to the mutant is applied and RE-RUN (a bound recomputing run per C5, not a stored boolean) -- the repair-run's own observed_attribution now matches A_i, so repair_verdict is PASS while the ORIGINAL conformance_verdict on this vector stays whatever it genuinely was.
